title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
text:
A monkey lived in a rose apple tree on the bank of a river. One day a crocodile came out of the water to rest beneath it, and the monkey threw him some of the sweet fruit. The two became friends. Every day the crocodile came to talk, and every day he took some fruit home to his wife.

The wife, however, grew jealous of the hours her husband spent away, and she reasoned that a monkey who ate such sweet fruit every day must have a very sweet heart. She told her husband she would only be happy if she could eat it. After much nagging, the crocodile gave in.

He invited the monkey to visit his home and carried him across the river on his back. In the middle of the water, feeling safe, he told the monkey the truth. The monkey kept calm. "Friend, why did you not say so earlier?" he said. "I keep my heart up in the rose apple tree. Take me back and I will fetch it for your wife."

The foolish crocodile swam back to the bank. The monkey leapt into his tree, climbed high out of reach and told the crocodile that their friendship was over.
lesson: Keep a cool head when someone you trusted turns on you; calm thinking can get you out of danger. And never let another person talk you into betraying a friend.
source: Panchatantra, Book IV (Loss of What Was Gained), frame story
